importance_ranking.reason: Extreme visual variation across sub-types — wooden cottage, steel cabin, glamping dome, container resort, bamboo hut — each has a distinct aesthetic. Buyers have a site concept and visual brief; wrong style = immediate skip before any text is read.

Structure material, floor area, furnishing level, and occupancy are the primary shortlisting gates. A listing without these specs cannot be evaluated for project fit — buyers cannot determine whether the unit matches their site requirement or guest capacity.

Indian hospitality developers compare per-sq-ft or per-unit rates across multiple suppliers after visual and spec shortlisting. Price varies substantially with structure material, floor area, and furnishing level — buyers need it to assess budget feasibility before contacting a seller.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom panel-build resort rooms are quoted per sq ft (dominant); standard factory-assembled cabin units are quoted per piece. Both units coexist in the market — price cannot be compared without knowing which unit applies to a given listing.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece is a genuine market ambiguity between custom-build and factory-cabin sellers. A buyer comparing two listings cannot assess value without the unit being explicitly shown alongside the price.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand exists in the Indian portable resort market; the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by material, style, and price rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Portfolio of completed resort projects, pan-India delivery capability, and turnkey installation track record are evaluated during vendor selection — particularly for large multi-unit deployments. Company matters but only after visual, spec, and price shortlisting are complete.
